Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

have verb

with a past participle: I have seen

also has, ’ve, have done, have been, have been doing, present perfect

classical

Catull. 9.5: vēnistī. ō mihi nūntiī beātī!
Ter. And. 139: Quid fēcī?

vīdī, fēcī, amāvī

the perfect tense: no auxiliary

I have seen, done, loved

One Latin tense does the work of “I have seen” and “I saw”. Passives and deponents form it with sum: victī sumus, we have been beaten (see be).

Other words

  • jam diū, jam dūdum (+ present) — I have been …ing (for a long time)

    adverb with the present tense · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.9.1: jam diū ignōrō quid agās; Ter. Eun. 816: Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.

    What began in the past and still goes on stands in the present, as in French: “my mind has long been on the dishes”.

  • habeō (+ perfect participle) — have (something) done, found out, settled (cognitum habeō)

    habeō with the perfect passive participle agreeing with its object · also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 58.1: compertum ego habeō (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 13.17.3: sī nōndum eum satis habēs cognitum (Lewis & Short)

    Stresses the state reached. Lewis & Short derives the Romance perfect from it (j’ai vu, ho veduto); in classical Latin it is not yet a tense, and “I have seen” is vīdī.

Examples

  • vēnistī. ō mihi nūntiī beātī!

    You’ve come! Oh, happy news for me!Catull. 9.5

  • Quid fēcī? quid commeruī aut peccāvī, pater?

    What have I done? What have I deserved, how have I gone wrong, father?Ter. And. 139

  • Periī hercle: nōmen perdidī.

    Oh no: I’ve forgotten the name.Ter. Ph. 386

  • cūr, inquit, turbulentam fēcistī mihi aquam bibentī?

    “Why,” he said, “have you muddied the water I’m drinking?”Phaedr. 1.1.5–6

  • Tum pol ego et oleum et operam perdidī.

    Then I’ve wasted both my oil and my effort.Plaut. Poen. 332b

  • jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis

    for a long time now I haven’t known how you are; you never writeCic. Fam. 7.9.1

  • Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.

    My mind has been on the dishes for ages.Ter. Eun. 816

See also had, be, will.

SourcesLewis & Short: habeo · Lewis & Short: jamdudum · Lewis & Short: diu

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
